stories.headline: Bangladesh has millions of small firms. Why do so few become exporters?
stories.summary: Bangladesh's 2024 Economic Census counted 11.7 million economic units employing more than 30.6 million people. Estimates put the share at around 25%, but the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics (BBS) produces no SME-specific export account and customs data are not linked systematically to firm size.
stories.why_it_matters: Key fact to remember: Bangladesh's 2024 Economic Census counted 11.7 million economic units employing more than 30.6 million people. This is the one to carry into BCS/Bank questions on the economy and banking.
stories.exam_facts: World Bank data show that the share of firms exporting fell from 25% to 13% over roughly a decade, while frontier firms' share of export revenue rose from 37% to 69%. Even so, India can show that the number of exporting MSMEs increased from 52,849 in 2020–21 to 173,350 in 2024–25. Zaidi Sattar, chairman of the Policy Research Institute, estimates, according to its research, Bangladesh's average nominal protection rate for FY2027 at 28%, half of it arising from para-tariffs.
